content:
Hi! I'm opening this thread following a suggestion from @Anatole Dedecker on PR #35559. That PR adds some API for WeakSpace and WeakDual for normed spaces.

I had originally introduced instBornology instances for both types, but ended up removing them since I could prove everything I needed without them. The reviewer raised the point that adding them would be a real design choice that deserves discussion, so here we are.

The two cases are a bit different:

WeakDual 𝕜 E
The natural candidate is the von Neumann bornology induced by the weak-* topology, which concretely is the pointwise bornology (sets bounded pointwise on E). The alternative is the norm bornology (operator norm bounded sets). These two don't agree in general: Banach-Steinhaus tells us they coincide when E is complete, but not otherwise. So the question is: which should be the instBornology instance?

WeakSpace 𝕜 E
This case is less subtle: norm-boundedness and weak-boundedness agree in full generality (no completeness assumption needed). But this is still a non-trivial theorem, so making it the instance would require some work to set up properly.

I'm happy to implement either instance (or both), I just want to make sure we settle on the right design before putting in the work.

I would expect weak-boundedness, but I have not really thought about it. The main reason I see is that otherwise it would be a pain (or another type synonym) to use weak-boundedness if ever needed. Also I would think that the proof that these bornologies coincide would be formalized as the statement that the identity is a bounded map.

Moritz Doll said:

otherwise it would be a pain (or another type synonym) to use weak-boundedness if ever needed

No, because this is just docs#Bornology.IsVonNBounded ! This is precisely why I don't really have an opinion myself: in the context of TVSs we just use the canonical notion of boundedness defined by the topology.

On the other hand it can be argued that, in the normed setting, it would be useful to say "this set of WeakDual k E is norm-bounded", e.g to conveniently state some concrete versions of Banach-Alaoglu, which would justify using Bounded for norm-boundedness and IsVonNBounded for weak/weak-star boundedness

I think the Bornology instance should be the norm bornology, as we already have a spelling for the other one, and otherwise we always have to writeIsBounded (preimage of some set under the identity map)

I think this is reasonable from a practical standpoint, though I note that (1) it is a bit morally wrong hence should be well-documented and (2) in general, when E is a TVS, you also care about subsets of WeakSpace E which are bounded for the original topology, and there you can't reuse the same trick

Here is a PR with bornology of WeakDual. It registers bornology instance as agreed above (added detailed comments in several palces), adds some API and adds general theorem isVonNBounded_iff_pointwise_bounded and isBounded_iff_isVonNBounded in complete case.
I'll work on bornology of WeakSpace in the meantime and open a PR when the first one get's merged.
